items.title: What Makes Ruby So Fun to Learn?
items.summary:
Join David A. Black and Joseph Leo III for a first look at The Well-Grounded Rubyist, Fourth Edition, their newly updated guide to writing Ruby with confidence and clarity. In this video, the authors talk about how the book has evolved over fifteen years, what’s new in the Ruby 3.4 era, and why understanding Ruby’s core ideas matters more than memorizing every method in the standard library.

The book focuses on the parts of Ruby that shape how experienced Rubyists think:
• Ruby’s object model—classes, modules, message passing, and the small details that make the language feel natural once you see how the pieces fit
• Built-in types like strings, arrays, hashes, symbols, and numerics, shown through examples you can apply right away
• Everyday tools such as RubyGems, blocks, functional patterns, mixins, regular expressions, and I/O
• Bigger concepts like reflection, threading, recursion, and how Ruby decides which method to call when you send a message

David and Joseph designed this edition to feel like a guided tour of the language. It’s friendly, readable, and full of “Oh, that finally makes sense” moments. If you’re learning Ruby for the first time or coming back to it after a few years, this edition gives you the foundation you need to write clear, expressive code—and to enjoy the process.

📘 Save 40% with code WATCHBLACK540 at https://hubs.la/Q03Wg3JB0

items.title: What does ancient bridge building and AI have in common?
items.summary:
Distinguished Scientist John Jumper explains how confidence in AI tools for science can come from seeing them perform reliably – similar to ancient builders constructing safe bridges without knowing the equations of their engineering.

He shares his journey from helping develop AlphaFold and being awarded a Nobel Prize, to accelerating science with AI – all on our podcast with @fryrsquared

items.title: The truth about working for yourself in AI
items.summary:
A lot of people ask what it’s actually like to work for yourself. I shared my take a few weeks ago, but it’s always refreshing to hear someone else’s lived reality. My friend @ShawhinTalebi  built an incredible AI education community and now teaches full-time, just like we do at Towards AI. And his experience? Surprisingly similar to mine.

When he transitioned from being a data scientist at Toyota to becoming an entrepreneur, he realized something big: the work stays almost the same — you’re still building, managing projects, solving problems. But the job changes. Because suddenly, around 33% of your time is spent on something you never worry about as an employee: client acquisition.

As your brand and company grow, your role shifts. You move from hands-on engineering to consulting, then to managing others, and eventually… you become a salesperson. Your main job becomes finding opportunities, closing deals, and keeping the business alive.

It’s still incredibly rewarding — but it’s a different game.

I’m Louis-François, PhD dropout, now CTO & co-founder at Towards AI. Follow me for tomorrow’s no-BS AI roundup 🚀

#entrepreneurship #ai #aieducation
